claim: Amazon Route 53 Global Resolver became generally available on 2026-03-09, available across 30 AWS Regions with IPv4 and IPv6 DNS query traffic, after a preview in 11 AWS Regions.
question: When did Route 53 Global Resolver become generally available?

evidence.quote: Posted on: Mar 9, 2026 Today, AWS announced the general availability of Amazon Route 53 Global Resolver, an internet-reachable anycast DNS resolver that delivers easy, secure, and reliable DNS resolution for authorized clients from anywhere.
Global Resolver is now available across 30 AWS Regions, with support for both IPv4 and IPv6 DNS query traffic.

Previewed at re:Invent 2025 in 11 AWS Regions, Global Resolver gives authorized clients in your organization anycast DNS resolution of public internet domains and private domains associated with Route 53 private hosted zones — from any location.

note: d13-089. Record dates only; keep out of questions.

claim: On 2025-11-19 Amazon Route 53 added AWS PrivateLink support for API requests to the route53.amazonaws.com service endpoint, so workloads can make changes to hosted zones, records and health checks without using the public internet.
question: What does Route 53 support for AWS PrivateLink let a VPC reach privately?

values.display: API requests to the route53.amazonaws.com service endpoint

qualifiers.condition: Customers outside US East (N. Virginia) use cross-Region interface VPC endpoints.

evidence.quote: Posted on: Nov 19, 2025 Amazon Route 53 now supports AWS PrivateLink for API requests to the route53.amazonaws.com service endpoint, allowing your AWS workloads to make changes to critical DNS infrastructure, including hosted zones, records, and health checks, without using the public internet.

Customers outside the US East (N. Virginia) Region can use cross-region Interface VPC endpoints to natively connect to Route53 from other Regions, without the need to send traffic over the public internet or set up inter-region connectivity like VPC peering.

note: d13-112. The post is about API requests only; it does not say anything about how DNS queries are answered (demand part 'does it change how DNS queries are answered': not found in this post).

claim: On 2025-11-21 Amazon Route 53 added dual stack support for the Route 53 DNS service API endpoint at route53.global.api.aws, and the existing IPv4 API endpoint stays available for backwards compatibility.
question: When did the Route 53 API endpoint get IPv6 and dual stack support?

qualifiers.scope: Amazon Route 53 DNS service API endpoint

evidence.quote: Posted on: Nov 21, 2025 Starting today, Amazon Route 53 supports dual stack for the Route 53 DNS service API endpoint at route53.global.api.aws, enabling you to connect from Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6), Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4), or dual stack clients.
The existing Route 53 DNS service IPv4 API endpoint will remain available for backwards compatibility.

note: API endpoint only; DNS answers are not affected.
